layout.title: How a traffic light works

shows.does: one red lamp hangs from a wire over the lane and glows red
a car rolls right past the small red lamp without stopping while a woman waits on the corner
the signal on its mast arm with a black backplate glows red over the lane
the red never changes and cars pile up nose to tail at the line
the green lamp lights and the queue drives off
the green stays on and a car streams past the woman waiting at the curb
a gray controller box appears by the pole and switches the lamp from green to red
a glowing outline traces the gray box and its door opens on the blinking modules
the box jumps from green straight to red and the second car rear-ends the first
the yellow lamp lights before the red and the dent is gone
on yellow the cars race on and shoot across the crosswalk past the waiting woman
every lamp holds red for a moment
at night one red car waits alone at the red on an empty road
a wire loop appears in the lane, its field rings under the car, the lamp turns green and the car goes
the loop feels only the first car while a long line of cars backs up behind it
a second loop glows farther back in the lane, the lamp turns green and the whole line drives off
the long green stays on and a taxi passes the woman still waiting on the corner
a push button appears on a post and the woman presses it, the lamp turns red
a storm rolls in with rain and the signal falls back to blinking red
a battery cabinet appears beside the controller, its lights blink and the lamps cycle again as the storm clears
a fire truck pulls up and waits at the red
a sensor appears on the pole, the lamp turns green and the fire truck drives through
the lamp turns red, two cars wait at the line and the woman steps out to cross
the signal runs its cycle over the street

layout.why: A street corner with a signal on its mast arm over the lane going away, its gray controller on the sidewalk and a woman waiting to cross. It opens close on one red lamp on a wire, then each fix lands on the signal itself (mast arm, green, controller, yellow, all-red, loops, button, battery, fire truck sensor) with the queue, the crash and the woman as the visible consequences; it ends with the woman stepping out on red.

sentences.text: If you hang a red lamp over a road, you have a traffic light.
But one small lamp is easy to miss, so cars roll through.
So you mount it on a mast arm with a backplate.
But now the red never changes, so cars pile up.
So you add a green lamp, and cars go.
But the green never ends, and the woman cannot cross.
So you add a box that switches green to red.
This is a signal controller.
But the box jumps straight to red, and cars crash.
So you add a yellow lamp that warns drivers first.
But drivers racing the yellow shoot into the crosswalk.
So you hold every lamp red for a moment.
But at night, that red makes one lone car wait.
So you cut a wire loop that feels its metal.
But the loop feels only the first car, so lines grow.
So a second loop farther back stretches the green.
But longer greens keep the woman waiting on the corner.
So you add a button that she presses to cross.
But the button needs power, and a storm cuts it.
So you add a battery that keeps the lamps running.
But running lamps still stop a fire truck at the red.
So a sensor turns it green for the truck.
Now the lamp turns red, and the woman crosses.
Congratulations, you have built a traffic light.

recurring.what: a woman waiting to cross at the corner
